backgrounds.name: Railway signalman
bios: Spent decades in a signal box at the train station. Still keeps railway time.
Railway signalman. Was on shift the night the Silence began.

habits.text: Checks a stopped wristwatch every few minutes.
Sorts the bunker's chores into a strict timetable.
Whistles the old departure signal on good days.

rescueLines: Thought nobody was listening anymore.
Thanks. Over.
Signal received. Coming in.
Keep the line open for me.

backgrounds.name: Teenager on their own
bios: Seventeen. Survived alone in an empty neighborhood. Won't say how.
A teenager who waited for family that never came back.

habits.text: Drums on every surface. Constantly.
Sleeps with shoes on, ready to run.
Asks the same question twice to make sure the answer holds.

rescueLines: Wait, there's really a bunker? With food?
Ok. I'm coming. Don't ask about my family.
Is this real? Someone's actually there?
Don't hang up. Please.

backgrounds.name: Nurse
bios: Worked at the Municipal Hospital until the very last day, by candlelight at the end.
A nurse who kept the ward running for weeks after the Silence.

habits.text: Checks everyone's forehead for fever, uninvited.
Keeps a tally of who ate and who didn't.
Hums old love songs while folding bandages.

rescueLines: Oh, thank goodness. Is anyone hurt over there?
I'm coming. Put the water on.
A bunker. With people. I'll bring what's left of my kit.
Hold on, I'm on my way.

backgrounds.name: Trucker
bios: Crossed the country three times in a truck. Has every road memorized.
Long-haul trucker. Was halfway across the country when the radio went quiet.

habits.text: Sleeps sitting up, like in a cab.
Draws road maps on any flat surface.
Taps the steering-wheel rhythm on the table while thinking.

rescueLines: Bunker? Never heard of you. Fine. Where do I park?
Coming in.
Been driving in circles for weeks. Give me a direction.
Got it. On my way.

backgrounds.name: Schoolteacher
bios: Taught third grade at the school down the road for twenty years.
A schoolteacher who still corrects everyone's grammar out of habit.

habits.text: Writes the date on the wall every morning.
Claps twice to get attention. It works.
Keeps a list of everyone's birthdays.

rescueLines: Good afternoon. I hope I'm not interrupting.
I'll be there shortly.
Finally, an adult voice. I'm coming.
Please be patient, I walk slowly.

backgrounds.name: Mechanic
bios: Fixed industrial machines for a living. Hands always black with grease.
A mechanic who kept a generator running alone for months.

habits.text: Takes things apart just to see how they work.
Keeps a screw in each pocket. Just in case.
Listens to the generator like a doctor with a stethoscope.

rescueLines: You've got a generator? Is it making a rattling noise?
Never mind. I'm coming.
Took me a week to rig this radio. Glad it worked.
Heading your way.

backgrounds.name: Cook
bios: Ran the canteen at the dam. Fed two hundred workers a day.
A cook who can make a meal out of three cans and a prayer.

habits.text: Smells every can before opening it.
Saves the best portion for whoever's been out longest.
Talks to the stove. Says it helps.

rescueLines: Do you have a kitchen? Any kitchen?
Good. I'm coming.
I'm hungry and I'm tired, but I can cook.
Wait for me.

backgrounds.name: Street musician
bios: Played guitar on the train lines for spare change. Knows a song for everything.
A street musician whose guitar was confiscated the night before the Silence.

habits.text: Hums the same four notes while working.
Taps rhythms on pipes to hear how the bunker sounds.
Writes lyrics on the back of ration labels.

rescueLines: A human voice. You don't know how good that sounds.
I'm coming. I'll bring a song.
Static, static, static, and then you.
On my way.
